name: Shoulder external rotation at 90°
instructions: Lie on your back, upper arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°.
Let the hand fall back toward the floor behind your head without arching your back.
Estimate the forearm angle: 0° is pointing at the ceiling, 90° is flat on the floor.

name: Shoulder internal rotation at 90°
instructions: Same start position: on your back, arm out at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°.
Rotate the hand forward and down toward your hip.
Stop as soon as the front of the shoulder starts lifting off the floor, and estimate the angle from vertical.

name: Apley scratch test
instructions: Stand tall. Reach one hand over the shoulder and down your back, palm toward you.
Bring the other hand up your back from below, palm facing out.
Measure the gap between the fingertips. Enter a negative number if they overlap.
The side you log is the arm that goes over the top.

name: Wall overhead reach
instructions: Stand with heels, bum, upper back and head against a wall, feet a small step forward.
Keep your lower back close to the wall and raise straight arms overhead.
Pick the score that matches what happens.

scoreLabels: Hands touch the wall, but only by arching the back
Hands touch the wall with the back flat
Easy: hands touch flat with room to spare

name: Seated hip internal rotation
instructions: Sit tall on the end of a bench, knees bent 90° and together.
Keeping the thigh still, swing the foot outward.
Estimate the shin angle from vertical without leaning your body.

name: Seated hip external rotation
instructions: Sit tall on the end of a bench, knees bent 90°.
Keeping the thigh still, swing the foot inward across the other leg.
Estimate the shin angle from vertical without leaning your body.

name: Deep squat hold
instructions: Feet about shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Sink into the deepest squat you can with heels flat on the floor.
Time how long you can hold it comfortably, without holding on to anything.

name: Thomas test (hip flexors)
instructions: Sit right on the end of a bench, then roll back while hugging one knee to your chest.
Let the other leg hang over the end of the bench and relax.
Watch the hanging thigh. The side you log is the hanging leg.

scoreLabels: Thigh stays clearly above the bench
Thigh nearly flat, or the knee straightens out
Thigh rests flat with the knee bent

name: Knee-to-wall
instructions: Half-kneel facing a wall, front foot pointing straight at it.
Drive the knee forward to touch the wall while keeping the heel down.
Slide the foot back until it's the furthest distance where you can still touch. Measure toe to wall.
